title: Tiered connection pool with hedging and progressive degradation for downstream resilience
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Services backed by Redis/Kafka/Postgres occasionally cause production P95/P99 latency spikes and SLO breaches when downstream clusters experience transient overload or fail partialy. Current single-tier connection pools and naive timeouts cause head-of-line blocking, global tail latency amplification, and cascading failures across regions.

Goal: Implement a composable, tiered connection pool + hedging + progressive degradation strategy that: preserves regional SLOs, prevents dependency overload, enables graceful degradation of non-critical features, and gives ops quick kill-switches for incidents. Provide runtime knobs, observability, and a safe rollout plan.

Scope: client-side (service) connection pooling behavior, regional hedging policy, circuit breaker rules, load-shedding policies, and graceful fallback patterns per downstream type (Redis, Kafka, Postgres). Integrations: runtime request router, telemetry pipelines (Console), and Dedicated/Private deployments for configuration surface.

Non-goals: Replacing remote datastore HA/replication strategies or deep changes in downstream server-side configs.

Success metrics (SLIs):
- API P95 latency for critical routes stays <= 120ms in steady-state and during injected downstream faults.
- Error rate for critical routes stays < 0.5% while the error budget is positive.
- Controlled degradation: non-critical features should be shed with < 5% churn to critical paths during overload.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive hedging reduces tail latency but increases load on downstream; mitigate with tokenized hedging budget and per-region reserve pools.
- Larger connection pools reduce queueing but raise downstream concentration; use adaptive pool sizing with a capped reserve for burst traffic.
- Stale-read fallbacks (Redis/DB) can return outdated data; only allowed behind explicit feature flags and with documented TTL/semantics.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after on-call incident where cross-region Redis failover caused 4x P95 increase. Initial spike analysis attached to Confluence link.
2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Spike repro in staging using downstream-latency-injector. Determined head-of-line blocking in global pool was main contributor. Drafted tiered pool prototype for review.
2026-03-05 - PM review (Sofia Gupta): Prioritize critical-route protection and safe defaults for Hosted customers. Ask: ensure config surface is limited for self-serve to avoid footguns.
2026-03-06 - Design review (Ravi Patel): Recommended per-tenant reserve pool minima and visible backpressure metrics in Console. Suggested stale-read UX text for degraded responses.
2026-03-08 - Security review request: sent initial design; no blocking issues but want KMS integration check if we persist any policy blobs.
progress_updates: 2026-03-04 - Prototype: Implemented tiered connection pool (hot/reserve) in service runtime; reserve pool is isolated and only used when latency budget is breached.
2026-03-06 - Hedging: Added conservative hedging with token-bucket rate limit (default 5% of requests) and per-endpoint override. Hedged attempts limited to 1 replica.
2026-03-07 - Circuit breakers: Added per-downstream/per-region CBs with trip on both error-rate and latency-surge signals. Added auto-reset backoff multiplier and manual overrides via Console.

2026-03-09 - Policies: Implemented progressive load-shedding policy: soft-shed non-critical routes first, then degrade cache TTLs before blocking critical routes; introduced feature flags for stale-read fallbacks.
2026-03-10 - Observability: Hooked new metrics to Console: pool utilization, hedging budget consumption, shed decisions, CB state transitions, and downstream fanout counts.
decision_log: 2026-03-05 - Decision: Use three-tier pool (hot, warm, reserve) instead of simple dynamic resizing to provide predictable isolation. (agreed by Eng/Design)
2026-03-06 - Decision: Limit hedging concurrency to 1 extra replica and require hedging budget token to be consumed; hedging disabled for write paths by default.
2026-03-07 - Decision: Circuit breaker triggers require both error-rate and sustained latency over baseline to avoid noisy CB flips on transient blips.
2026-03-08 - Decision: Non-blocking stale-read fallback allowed for read-only endpoints behind explicit flag; must present header 'X-Degraded-Response: true' and telemetry event.
2026-03-09 - Rollout decision: Canary on 5% of traffic in us-west first, monitor P95 and shed rate; rollback if P95 > 150ms or shed rate > 2x expected thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Tiered pool implemented and configurable (hot/warm/reserve) with defaults documented.
Hedging + token-bucket policy implemented with safe defaults and per-endpoint opt-out.
Circuit breakers evaluate combined latency+error signals and expose state to Console + telemetry.
Progressive load-shedding policy correctly demotes features by priority and emits shed events to metrics.
E2E chaos tests demonstrate no SLO regression for critical routes in 5 simulated downstream failure patterns.
Runbook and kill-switch are documented and tested in on-call run-through.
